title: hotfix: slo-enforcer regional failover + load-shedding stability
author: Priya Kaur
description: Motivation: production incidents in multiple regions during a traffic spike revealed two issues: 1) the SLO enforcer backoff and circuit-breaker ordering allowed cross-region failovers to oscillate under bursty load, and 2) aggressive global load-shedding suppressed low-latency prioritized traffic. This hotfix tightens ordering guarantees in the enforcer, adds a short stabilization window before regional failover, and refines load-shedding to respect priority classes. Summary of changes: updated enforcer state machine to prefer local capacity for an additional stabilization period (200ms by default), made circuit-breaker backoff smoothing configurable per-region, added a priority-aware load-shedding policy that uses token-budget accounting, fixed race in failover decision path that could double-count in-flight tokens, added unit and integration tests, and updated deployment docs and runtime feature flag gate. Backport: none required for current release cadence; targeted at main and will be cherry-picked to release/2026-02 for immediate rollout. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind slo_enforcer_stabilization_v2; staged rollout to 20% of traffic in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 for 24h, monitor SLOs and failover metrics, expand to all regions if stable. Rollback: flip feature flag off and revert regional backoff config. Testing: extensive unit tests added, integration test validates failover ordering under synthetic bursts, e2e canary ran in staging and passed. Ops notes: adjust ops dashboard to surface new metric slo_enforcer.failover_stabilization_window_ms and ensure alerts for sustained regional thrashing are set to 5m window. Changelog: critical reliability hotfix; no API changes.
